top.title: Glastonbury girls cross country has won 14 Class LL titles. Here's how the Guardians keep winning
top.description: Glastonbury took the Class LL championship during the CIAC Girls Cross Country Championships held Saturday, October 31, 2026 at Wickham Park in Manchester. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) When you talk about high school girls cross country in Connecticut, Glastonbury gets mentioned pretty often, and with good reason. This season, the Guardians won both the Class LL and State Open team championships, while junior Lauren Parrett claimed the individual titles in both races. Glastonbury earned its first state championship in 2004 in Class LL. Since then, the Guardians have won 13 more Class LL team championships, 14 overall. The program won its first State Open team championship in 2007, on the heels of a fourth straight Class LL title. The Guardians have captured eight State Open team championships. On 11 occasions, a Glastonbury runner has won a Class LL individual state championship. A Guardian has claimed the State Open individual title five times. Since 2004, the program has had an individual or team state champion in 17 of 23 seasons. What makes Glastonbury cross country successful So the question is, why is Glastonbury so good? "We do have a lot of good runners who have come through," said Parrett after she won the State Open on Nov. 5 at Manchester's Wickham Park. "I think a big part of it is us supporting each other all the time. I think it's our training, too." Parrett added: "We do a lot of training leading up to this, and we work hard for the positions and awards we get." Parrett is just one of multiple star runners who have come through the program. When talking about Parrett, head coach Brian Collins mentioned some of those other big names. They included Lindsay Crevoiserat, Kristin Mitchell and Brooke Strauss. More on all of them later. "As a freshman, I think (Parrett) was ninth in New England. She ran some good times here in her freshman and sophomore years," Collins said. "You don't know how much better some of these kids will get. Sometimes they stabilize because it's hard at that point." This is where Collins started to explain how the program reaches a championship level. "We're a low-mileage school. We do 29, 30, 31 miles a week," Collins said. "(Parrett) goes off in another program and does 35, 40, 45 miles a week, would she be a little bit stronger and better? Yes. We don't do that because at that point, the risk of injury is greater at that age. "People always think that we're running 40, 45, 50 miles a week. Our kids don't. If you do the workouts the right way, whether it be the harder days, the long-run days, the easier days or whatever, we found something that worked for us over the last 22, 23 years. We tweak it a little bit here and there, and you know the old saying, if it's not broke, don't fix it." Passing it on Parrett took the mantle from Strauss, a three-time individual state champion (sophomore State Open in 2022, senior Class LL and Open in 2024) who now runs for UConn. top.title: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams
top.description: Ospreys now play home games at St Helen's [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ospreys says a report they commissioned into Welsh rugby concludes that the proposed cut of four professional clubs to three should not happen. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has said it intends to drop a side by 2028, with the decision made by next summer. With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales. Ospreys asked experts at Sheffield Hallam University to look at the issues and they produced the "Welsh rugby data report". That found "the independent analysis of the data does not logically lead to a conclusion that the removal of one professional team in Wales is a strategic move grounded in evidence". Ospreys say they back the need to keep four clubs. The report has not yet been published in full. That will not be done until later this month when it will be sent to the regions and WRU. Why four clubs should be maintained The Ospreys highlight the reasons the report concludes the number of professional clubs in Wales should remain at four. Derbies: The report claims fixtures between the four Welsh clubs generated 48% of league attendances at home games in Wales from 2012 to 2026. With three clubs, those fixtures would fall from 12 derbies a season to six. Players: Removing one team would create what the report calls a "bottleneck", with fewer elite playing opportunities in Wales and a greater risk of more Welsh players moving to clubs outside Wales. Wales: The report finds that Wales have recorded higher Six Nations finishes in the seasons when the Welsh clubs have performed well. All four clubs contribute: Over the period the report records Cardiff with the highest average attendances, Scarlets as the leading Welsh club in the European Cup and Dragons with the highest stadium utilisation, alongside the Ospreys' record in the league and in supplying most players to Wales and the Lions. What has not been included in great depth in the initial findings are the financial constraints or how keeping four teams can be afforded. The WRU has reported recent losses of £18m and says it has to reduce its spend on professional rugby from £26m to £20m by 2028. The four sides currently receive about £6.5m each. The Ospreys report follows the Keystone report that was commissioned by the WRU who said it outlined data why Welsh rugby needs to cut a side. top.description: 'We have to concentrate on our game' - Darcie Greene previews FA Cup challenge Leeds United Women defender Darcie Greene is looking forward to Sunday's FA Cup Second Round tie against Norton & Stockton Ancients, as the Whites aim to continue their recent winning form. Following the end of their impressive 10-game winning streak against title rivals AFC Fylde Women, Simon Wood's side have responded with three consecutive victories and will be hoping to make it four this weekend. Ahead of the cup clash, Greene discussed the significance of maintaining momentum. "I feel like it is very important to continue our winning form, we want to ensure we are consistent with our performances so that we are continuing to build confidence within the team. "We have already faced Norton this season in the league. We know they are very strong defensively and a very hard team to play. We’ve got to concentrate on our game and make sure we are prepared. "FA Cup games are always an exciting challenge and winning gives us the opportunity to be in the hat for the next round. It gives us a break from the league action and it allows us to be challenged by playing different opposition." Reflecting on her own performances this season, including finding the net in last weekend's victory over Durham Cestria, the defender explained her desire to keep growing and contributing to the team. "No matter how well I play, I will always look at the areas in the game where I need to improve or what I could do differently. top.title: Matt Henry and Will Young dismantle India as New Zealand register a 244-run win
top.description: New Zealand kept the series alive with a commanding 244-run win over India in Friday's fourth one-day international at Mount Maunganui, driven by a century from Will Young and a six-wicket haul by Matt Henry, who dismissed the touring side for 89. Although trailing 2-1 in the five-match contest and unable to claim an overall series victory, the home team can still secure a draw should they win Sunday’s final fixture at the same ground. Rain had forced the abandonment of the third game. Set a target of 334, India endured a terrible start when fast bowler Henry reduced them to 0-3 during a devastating opening over, dismissing Rohit Sharma , Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer in quick succession. Ruturaj Gaikwad was removed soon after, though a stubborn 44-run stand between Ishan Kishan (27) and Axar Patel (21), alongside a rapid 21 from Naman Dhir, prevented India from suffering a record-breaking run defeat. Henry claimed three further victims to wrap up the innings, bowling India out for their sixth-lowest total in ODI history. Will Young celebrating hitting a century off 88 balls (Getty) At the start of the day, opener Young recovered from earlier scores of 9 and 6 in the series to make a career-best 125 off 108 balls to the gall of India who dropped him twice on the way to registering his fifth century in the format. The 33-year-old capitalised on sloppy Indian fielding after Rohit and Kishan dropped catches off consecutive balls during the second over of the innings. Young received solid support from Tim Seifert, who scored 58, and Finn Allen, who added 41, while India's bowling attack saw Patel, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi take two wickets apiece. India were missing captain Shubman Gill and batter KL Rahul, both of whom are sidelined for the rest of the ODI series to prepare for Wednesday’s two-test series against New Zealand.

top.description: Tottenham consider January loan recall for Mikey Moore amid Rangers return talk Expectations were high when Mikey Moore joined 1. FC Köln on loan from Tottenham Hotspur towards the end of the summer transfer window, but the 19-year-old's spell in Germany hasn't gone according to plan so far. Moore is still waiting for his first goal in Germany, having started six of the nine games he has played in all competitions for the Billy Goats. Given Moore's struggles to establish himself in the Bundesliga, Tottenham and Köln could agree to terminate his loan six months early in January, according to a report from TEAMtalk. Such a move would allow Spurs to explore alternative options for the teenager in a bid to find him a destination that would be a better fit than Köln has been so far. Moore enjoyed great success at Rangers last season, but the Scottish side are not actively pursuing a return for him. Nevertheless, should his loan spell be terminated early, both Moore and Rangers “would be forced to consider it”, the report suggests. No decision will be made just yet, however, with Moore's form between now and the January transfer window set to influence what happens next.

top.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
top.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. nigeria.title: Makinde scores Tinubu administration 34 per cent
nigeria.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has scored President Bola Tinubu’s administration 34 per cent, saying the government has failed to secure the support of a majority of Nigerians. Makinde gave the assessment during an interview with Arise Television, where he was asked to evaluate the administration’s performance in infrastructure, diplomacy and economic growth. He likened the score to the percentage of Nigerians who supported Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, arguing that the President needed to win over those who voted against him to build a national consensus. “It’s just about the same percentage as the people that supported him in 2023, 34 per cent. You need the 66 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board. This is a national project,” he said. The governor also criticised what he described as pressure on elected officials to join the ruling All Progressives Congress, alleging that some governors were compelled to defect. “Look at what we’ve seen. You have the governors come to APC. If you don’t, you’ll be blackmailed,” he said. Makinde, who is seeking the presidency in 2027 under the Action Peoples Party (APM), also addressed whether he would accept defeat if the election was free, fair and credible. Responding to a question on whether he would concede defeat and retire to farming, the governor said he would accept the outcome if the electoral process met the required standards. “There are a few things that must happen. If the process is free, fair, and credible, yes, I will,” he said. However, when asked whether he would remain in the APM after the election, Makinde said his political future would depend on how Nigerians received his political agenda. “I may evaluate my political future depending on how Nigerians, you know, see this agenda,” he added. nigeria.description: Smartphone cameras have become increasingly sophisticated in 2026, with manufacturers competing to deliver sharper photographs, improved low-light performance and, particularly, better zoom capabilities. One of the biggest developments has been the introduction of more advanced periscope telephoto cameras, larger image sensors and optical zoom systems capable of capturing distant subjects without relying entirely on digital enlargement. These improvements have made it possible to photograph wildlife, sporting events, concerts, buildings and other distant subjects with a level of detail that was previously difficult to achieve with a smartphone. While several manufacturers advertise zoom capabilities of up to 100x or 120x, the actual quality of photographs at those magnifications varies considerably. Optical zoom, sensor size, optical image stabilisation and image processing are therefore more important considerations than the maximum zoom figure alone. Here are five smartphones with some of the best zoom camera systems available in 2026, based on their camera hardware and independent reviews. 1. Oppo Find X9 Ultra The Oppo Find X9 Ultra stands out as one of the most capable zoom smartphones of 2026, particularly because it features two dedicated telephoto cameras rather than relying on a single zoom lens. The smartphone comes with a 200-megapixel primary telephoto camera offering 3x optical zoom and a separate 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera capable of 10x optical zoom. The combination gives users greater flexibility when photographing subjects at different distances, from portraits and street photography to distant buildings, wildlife and performers at concerts. Its 10x optical zoom is particularly important because it allows the camera to magnify distant subjects using its dedicated optical hardware rather than simply enlarging pixels digitally. According to Digital Trends, the phone can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally. Its 200-megapixel telephoto camera also provides additional room for cropping images while retaining useful detail. The publication highlights the phone’s impressive telephoto sharpness, autofocus performance and ability to capture distant subjects. For people who regularly photograph sporting events, wildlife or concerts, the Find X9 Ultra is a particularly compelling option. 2. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra The Huawei Pura 80 Ultra is another smartphone that deserves recognition for its unusual approach to long-range photography. Its biggest attraction is a switchable dual-telephoto camera system that offers 3.7x and 9.4x optical zoom. Unlike conventional smartphones that use separate telephoto sensors for different magnification levels, Huawei developed a system in which two telephoto lenses share a large 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch sensor. Dramatic dispatch audio captured the initial callout for a shooting inside the gym just before 8 am (0100 GMT). Jeffery Carroll, Washington’s interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, identified as Matt Lambert, 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment. Lambert, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager, James Stuart, 46, in a packed gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighborhood. nigeria.title: Obi leads NDC supporters in singing old national anthem in Lagos
nigeria.description: Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), on Thursday joined party supporters in singing Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’, at a town hall meeting in Lagos. Obi, alongside Funso Doherty, the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, and other attendees, declined to stand for the recital of the current national anthem when prompted by the event anchor. The anchor subsequently switched to the old anthem, which Obi and the supporters sang together. During the recital, Obi faced the crowd with two fingers raised on both hands, forming a gesture associated with the NDC logo. A video of the incident, which has since circulated on social media, showed the party supporters enthusiastically singing the former national anthem. The development comes amid controversy surrounding the reintroduction of the old anthem by President Bola Tinubu. On May 29, 2024, Tinubu signed the National Anthem Bill into law, restoring ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as the country’s official anthem, replacing ‘Arise, O Compatriots’. The old anthem was first adopted at Nigeria’s independence on October 1, 1960, and remained in use until 1978, when it was replaced. Meanwhile, the town hall meeting was earlier disrupted when suspected thugs reportedly invaded the venue with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, forcing attendees to flee for safety. Obi previously secured victory in Lagos State during the 2023 presidential election as the Labour Party candidate, polling 582,354 votes against Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who received 572,606 votes. nigeria.title: US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy
nigeria.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. nigeria.title: ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader
nigeria.description: Decades of discrimination and extortion against Fulani herders are stoking the growing violence in northern Nigeria — unrest which will only swell until authorities tame the rampant corruption in the region, a bandit kingpin told AFP in a rare interview. Northwest and central Nigeria have for years been terrorised by gangs known locally as “bandits”, who raid villages, rustle cattle, conduct kidnappings and impose “taxes” on farmers and miners. The interview with one such gang leader came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, in a piece published Thursday, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and AFP northern Nigeria reporter Aminu Abubakar. “Years of injustices are what pushed Fulani herders into banditry. We were never criminals before,” a bandit leader named Babangida said. Banditry traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders. The conflict has spiralled from raids and revenge attacks into broader, complex criminality by gangs numbering from around a dozen to well into the hundreds. They have created a kidnapping economy that raises hundreds of thousands of dollars, and at times entered alliances with Nigerian jihadists. After months of negotiation, Babangida agreed to an interview in a remote Katsina state village, following the intervention of a former government peace negotiator. “Justice is the only way out. When justice is upheld, everyone will live in peace,” said the bandit, who asked only to be identified by his first name. In the meantime, violence reigns: last week, in neighbouring Zamfara state, bandits set fire to a home during a raid, killing a family of 12. Earlier this month, gunmen killed eight police officers, and in September, more than 80 people, mostly women, were kidnapped in Zamfara and Niger states — many while working their fields. Worsening insecurity has become a major issue in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. – Corruption – Clad in a blue kaftan, the 38-year-old passes for a normal villager, save for the Kalashnikov rifle in his hand. “No bandit just picked up a gun overnight and turned to violence. There is always a story behind it,” said Babangida, sheltering from the scorching heat under a neem tree. Babangida said he turned to banditry a decade ago after his family’s 97 cows were seized by a team of police and vigilantes. He described the raid as based on indiscriminate suspicions that all Fulani are bandits. He was forced to pay millions of naira (thousands of dollars) to post bail for his mother and brother. nigeria.title: INEC warns Okada riders against political violence in Oyo
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Oyo State against allowing politicians to use them as instruments of violence, thuggery and electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission urged members of transport unions to resist attempts to involve them in activities capable of undermining public peace and the credibility of the electoral process before, during and after the elections. The Oyo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Adeniran Tella, gave the warning on Thursday at the 2026 Day celebration of the Amalgamated Commercial Tricycle and Motorcycle Owners, Repairs and Riders Association of Nigeria (ACOMORAN), held alongside the launch of a book authored by the union’s chairman, Solomon Olugbode, at the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium, Oke-Ado, Ibadan. Tella, who was represented by the Head of INEC’s Information Unit, Olayiwola Awolowo, also urged members of the association to encourage their passengers and other members of the public to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). He stressed the importance of civic participation in the electoral process, saying commercial transport operators had a responsibility to protect democracy rather than allow themselves to be recruited into activities capable of threatening national security. “Let me be clear, do not allow yourselves to be used as instruments of violence or thuggery. The Nigeria Police Force has warned that the law will take its full course against anyone, no matter their status, who threatens public peace or engages in criminal conduct before, during or after the elections,” he said. Specifically, he charged ACOMORAN members to shun political violence, warning them against transporting weapons, money for vote-buying or individuals intending to disrupt the elections. “Your motorcycle or tricycle is a tool of livelihood, not a weapon of destruction. I urge you to remain politically neutral as a union,” he added. The INEC representative also cautioned the association against allowing its structures and operational resources to be deployed in support of any political party, noting that members retained the right to support candidates of their choice in their individual capacities. “While you have the right to support any candidate of your choice as individuals, the union’s infrastructure must never be hijacked to favour one party over another,” he said. He urged the transport operators to support INEC’s election logistics by ensuring the timely and safe movement of electoral materials and personnel whenever engaged by the commission. He also called on members to serve as voter education ambassadors by promoting peace, tolerance and responsible voting at motor parks and among their passengers. nigeria.title: Protesters block INEC chair’s vehicle in London, demand resignation
nigeria.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was confronted by protesters in London on Thursday over alleged irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The demonstrators surrounded the vehicle conveying Amupitan outside Chatham House, where he was expected to participate in a panel discussion on Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 polls. The protesters, believed to be Nigerians living abroad, shouted insults at the INEC chairman and accused the commission of abandoning its neutrality in favour of President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress. They also demanded Amupitan’s resignation, labelling INEC a “criminal organisation” over alleged duplicate voter registrations, questionable polling units and photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence. The demonstration followed mounting criticism of the commission after images and records purportedly showing suspicious entries in the preliminary voters’ register circulated publicly. INEC had acknowledged irregularities in the registration process and announced an investigation into the affected records, further fuelling the controversy. ‘Trust me I won’t fail you’ Speaking earlier at the event, Amupitan asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo has said that the state requires about 1,000 megawatts of electricity to adequately power its growing economy. Delivering the keynote address at the Electricity Market Investment Roundtable organised by the Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission (ASERC) in Awka, the governor lamented that Anambra currently receives only about 120 megawatts, describing the huge gap as both a major challenge and an investment opportunity. “Without electricity, there will be no manufacturing. Without energy, only little can happen. For us, it is very consequential. We are here to do business. Anambra is ready for business,” the governor declared. Soludo urged investors to take advantage of the numerous opportunities in the state’s electricity market, particularly those connected with the state’s proposed Mixed Industrial City and aerotropolis. The governor threw open the state’s electricity market to investors, declaring that Anambra is ready for business as it seeks to bridge a massive power deficit threatening its industrial and economic growth. To the participants at the summit, Soludo added: “Tell us when, where and how we can get the 1,000 megawatts. Let’s get the plan, a clear roadmap, actionable, verifiable roadmap. Anambra is a land of opportunities. This is a summit for closing deals. Let’s get it done. “Move beyond discussions and produce a practical, measurable and verifiable roadmap for closing the state’s electricity gap.” The governor reiterated his administration’s determination to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation in the electricity market. Chairman of Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission, ASERC, Professor Frank Okafor, commended the governor for driving innovation and reforms in the state’s energy sector. He acknowledged the substantial electricity deficit in Anambra, explaining that the roundtable was convened to bring stakeholders together to develop practical solutions to the challenge. “We are here to think together and come up with a solution that will help to overcome the challenge,” Okafor said. Former chairman of the Nigeria Communications Commission, NCC, Engr. Ernest Ndukwe, who chaired the event, noted that Governor Soludo has the capacity to deliver the changes required in the state’s electricity sector. nigeria.title: Swiss woman evacuated from Nigeria over Ebola discharged in Geneva
nigeria.description: A Swiss woman who contracted the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has been discharged from hospital in Geneva, Switzerland. The woman, who is the wife of a Swiss embassy employee in Abuja, was evacuated from Nigeria alongside her husband on October 26 after contracting the virus. Benoit Carpentier, spokesperson for the University Hospitals of Geneva (HUG), said the patient received supportive medical care, including hydration and management of potential complications associated with the disease. “The patient has recovered. She was discharged from hospital yesterday (Wednesday),” he told AFP, confirming a report by Tribune de Genève. The woman’s husband reportedly showed no symptoms of the disease, while his quarantine was lifted on November 4. Nigeria announced the Ebola case on October 20, confirming that it involved the Bundibugyo strain, the same variant responsible for the latest outbreak in the DRC. The strain remains a major public health concern as there is currently no specific approved treatment or vaccine against it. The outbreak was officially detected in the DRC in May and has since infected more than 11,000 people, with over 5,400 deaths recorded. Cases have also been detected in Uganda and Kenya, raising concerns about the spread of the disease across the region. nigeria.title: Nigeria taking religious violence more seriously after US CPC listing – Officials
nigeria.description: US State Department officials have said Nigeria is taking religious violence more seriously following its designation as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC) by President Donald Trump, but warned that more concrete action is needed to protect vulnerable communities and bring perpetrators to justice. The officials made the assessment on Thursday during a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s response to attacks on vulnerable communities since the US placed the country on its CPC list. President Trump redesignated Nigeria as a CPC over allegations of Christian persecution and genocide before the US military launched a missile strike against terrorist targets in Sokoto State on Christmas Day. Nigeria and the US have since entered into a military partnership targeting terrorists in the country’s northern region and established a joint working group to address Washington’s concerns over religious violence. The hearing was convened by Chris Smith, Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Africa Subcommittee, to examine Nigeria’s response to attacks on vulnerable communities following the CPC designation. Speaking at the hearing, Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, said the State Department had intensified engagements with Nigerian officials to address attacks against Christian communities and ensure accountability for perpetrators. He, however, acknowledged that the violence had persisted, stressing that Washington expected measurable improvements in security deployments, early responses to warnings of impending attacks and prosecution of those responsible. “We are expecting results — protection for Christian communities in the Middle Belt through increased Nigerian security and law enforcement deployments, more timely and effective responses to early warnings of impending attacks, accountability for perpetrators through stronger courts and security services, and deeper military-to-military cooperation,” he said. Garcia said the US was pursuing a coordinated approach to strengthening Nigeria’s security architecture through capacity building, expanded use of biometric data to identify perpetrators and financial action plans to disrupt terrorist financing networks. “Though Nigeria has reported progress, under Secretary Hooker made it clear in the joint working group second session that this pace is insufficient,” he added. Also speaking, Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour, said the US had continued to urge the Nigerian government to repeal blasphemy laws or, at the minimum, stop enforcing them. Barnes said Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a CPC had prompted the country to take religious violence and related concerns more seriously. “The government has reported leadership changes, strategically deployed military forces, and increased arrests and prosecutions,” he said. nigeria.title: Fasoranti’s death ends an era, says Akure communities
nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Akure Speaking Communities Development Initiative (ASCDI) has described the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, as the end of an era of wisdom, exemplary leadership, patriotism and selfless service to Akureland, Yorubaland and Nigeria. The group said the late elder statesman was a moral compass whose life and leadership inspired generations, describing his death as a profound loss to the people of Akure, the Yoruba nation and the country. In a condolence statement issued in Akure and signed by its Chairman, Air Commodore Adewale Ogunmodede (retd.), and Secretary, Dr Olawale Ademola, ASCDI said it received the news of his passing with profound sorrow. It described Fasoranti as an illustrious son of Akureland, a respected statesman and a distinguished Yoruba leader. “Pa Fasoranti was not merely an elder statesman; he was a moral compass, a symbol of courage, an embodiment of integrity, and a custodian of the cherished values and traditions of our people. “His life represented the finest ideals of community service, peaceful coexistence, justice, unity, and the pursuit of collective progress,” the statement said. The organisation noted that as leader of Afenifere and a prominent voice in national affairs, Fasoranti devoted much of his life to championing the interests of the Yoruba people, promoting democratic ideals and advocating fairness, equity and good governance in Nigeria. For the Akure Speaking Communities across Ifedore, Akure North and Akure South Local Government Areas of Ondo State, ASCDI said his death represented an immeasurable loss. It described him as a towering figure whose wisdom, experience and fatherly guidance inspired generations of leaders and community development advocates. “His enduring legacy reminds us that true greatness is measured not by personal accomplishments alone, but by the positive impact one makes on society and the values one leaves behind for succeeding generations,” it added. The group urged sons and daughters of Akure Speaking Communities, both at home and in the diaspora, to honour his memory by strengthening their commitment to unity, peaceful coexistence, cultural preservation and sustainable community development. It also extended its condolences to the Fasoranti family, the Deji and other royal fathers in the Akure Speaking Communities, the leadership and members of Afenifere, the Ondo State Government and people, as well as the Yoruba nation. “We pray that Almighty God grants the bereaved family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss and grants the departed patriarch eternal rest. “Although Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti may have departed this earthly realm, his ideals, sacrifices, wisdom, and contributions to humanity will remain indelibly engraved in the annals of our history,” the statement said. nigeria.title: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor
nigeria.description: By Emmma Nnadozie A 24-year-old student of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, has recounted how he narrowly escaped death during an off-campus party that claimed the lives of four students in Nsukka, Enugu State. The survivor, an Art Education student, said he lost consciousness after one of the participants vomited during the party, only to regain consciousness several hours later and discover his friends lying motionless on the floor. Recounting his experience with our Crime Editor, the student said the gathering was organised by his friend, David, to celebrate the completion of his final examinations. According to him, the host bought two bottles of alcoholic drinks, Magic Moment and Best, which they took to his residence at Hilltop, Nsukka, where about 10 people gathered for the celebration. He said the party started around 11:30 a.m., adding that the participants shared the drinks while engaging in a Truth and Dare game for entertainment. He narrated: “During the party, one of the participants started vomiting. I took him to the toilet and asked him to clean himself up. I then came out to clean the vomit on the floor. “After that, I suddenly lost consciousness. However, I noticed that my legs had become stiff, and I could no longer walk. “When I regained consciousness at about 9 p.m., I heard someone saying that a ghost was shaking. I woke up and managed to look into the parlour, where I saw the host and other participants lying on the floor.” The survivor said he immediately contacted a friend, who came to the house, saw their condition and left. He expressed disappointment that another person who reportedly arrived at the scene started recording them instead of making efforts to rescue them. He said he subsequently contacted another friend, who came and helped convey them to Bishop Shanahan Hospital and other hospitals in Nsukka for medical attention. Explaining the circumstances surrounding the gathering, the survivor said the participants were inside the parlour with the doors and windows shut, while a generator was operating outside in the corridor. nigeria.title: Regulators, private sector leaders, others to review local content growth
nigeria.description: Regulatory authorities, private sector leaders and legislators have concluded arrangement for a closed-door Local Content Roundtable to review Nigeria’s journey path of localizing its industries over the years. The engagement, driven by the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum 2026, is designed to shift the national conversation from indigenous participation to sustainable, in-country capacity development. It would also focus around the team: ‘‘Building Sustainable Local Capacity: Scaling Capability, Enabling Ownership and Funding Growth’’, and will confront the issue of physical, technological or intellectual capacity created in Nigeria since the inception of the policy in 2010. “Every year at PNC, we celebrate the percentage. This year, we wanted a room that explores what that percentage is made of, and how we build on it,” said Wemimo Oyelana, Portfolio and Country Director, dmg events, organizers of the meeting. He stated further: “The skills, technology and industrial capacity developed through projects over the past 16 years are real assets. The Roundtable will bring stakeholders together to define what lasting Nigerian capacity looks like, how it can be measured, and how we grow it at scale.” According to the organizers, PNC 2026 will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors and indigenous businesses to address the priorities shaping the next phase of Nigerian Content development. For operators and project developers, the discussions will examine how local capacity can support project delivery and long-term competitiveness. nigeria.title: My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain
nigeria.description: Flamingos captain, Harmony Chidi, has revealed how her mother initially opposed her ambition to become a professional footballer and wanted her to get married following the early death of her father. The 17-year-old, who led Nigeria to a historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, said her grandmother and foster father played crucial roles in keeping her football dream alive despite the opposition. Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to become the first African country to win the competition. Speaking in an interview with BBC Pidgin, Chidi said her mother was initially unwilling to allow her to pursue football after the death of her father, but her grandmother stood by her and encouraged her to continue. “When I started football, my mother didn’t want me to play. My father died early, so my mother wanted me to get married. It was my grandmother who stood by me and pushed me to play football. Unfortunately, my grandmother is late,” she said. The Bayelsa Queens striker also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, owner of her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, for providing the encouragement and support she needed to pursue her ambition. “It wasn’t easy until I met my foster father, Prince Chidi. He is the owner of my grassroots team, Imo Strikers, and he encourages me, making sure that I achieve my dream,” she added. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement. The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers. Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals. Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work. Individual cases point to Monero and bitcoin The closest official window into how the vendors were paid comes from the cases the Justice Department highlighted and from court papers posted with the announcement. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.title: Glastonbury girls cross country has won 14 Class LL titles. Here's how the Guardians keep winning
sports.description: Glastonbury took the Class LL championship during the CIAC Girls Cross Country Championships held Saturday, October 31, 2026 at Wickham Park in Manchester. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) When you talk about high school girls cross country in Connecticut, Glastonbury gets mentioned pretty often, and with good reason. This season, the Guardians won both the Class LL and State Open team championships, while junior Lauren Parrett claimed the individual titles in both races. Glastonbury earned its first state championship in 2004 in Class LL. Since then, the Guardians have won 13 more Class LL team championships, 14 overall. The program won its first State Open team championship in 2007, on the heels of a fourth straight Class LL title. The Guardians have captured eight State Open team championships. On 11 occasions, a Glastonbury runner has won a Class LL individual state championship. A Guardian has claimed the State Open individual title five times. Since 2004, the program has had an individual or team state champion in 17 of 23 seasons. What makes Glastonbury cross country successful So the question is, why is Glastonbury so good? "We do have a lot of good runners who have come through," said Parrett after she won the State Open on Nov. 5 at Manchester's Wickham Park. "I think a big part of it is us supporting each other all the time. I think it's our training, too." Parrett added: "We do a lot of training leading up to this, and we work hard for the positions and awards we get." Parrett is just one of multiple star runners who have come through the program. When talking about Parrett, head coach Brian Collins mentioned some of those other big names. They included Lindsay Crevoiserat, Kristin Mitchell and Brooke Strauss. More on all of them later. "As a freshman, I think (Parrett) was ninth in New England. She ran some good times here in her freshman and sophomore years," Collins said. "You don't know how much better some of these kids will get. Sometimes they stabilize because it's hard at that point." This is where Collins started to explain how the program reaches a championship level. "We're a low-mileage school. We do 29, 30, 31 miles a week," Collins said. "(Parrett) goes off in another program and does 35, 40, 45 miles a week, would she be a little bit stronger and better? Yes. We don't do that because at that point, the risk of injury is greater at that age. "People always think that we're running 40, 45, 50 miles a week. Our kids don't. sports.title: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams
sports.description: Ospreys now play home games at St Helen's [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ospreys says a report they commissioned into Welsh rugby concludes that the proposed cut of four professional clubs to three should not happen. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has said it intends to drop a side by 2028, with the decision made by next summer. With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales. Ospreys asked experts at Sheffield Hallam University to look at the issues and they produced the "Welsh rugby data report". That found "the independent analysis of the data does not logically lead to a conclusion that the removal of one professional team in Wales is a strategic move grounded in evidence". Ospreys say they back the need to keep four clubs. The report has not yet been published in full. That will not be done until later this month when it will be sent to the regions and WRU. Why four clubs should be maintained The Ospreys highlight the reasons the report concludes the number of professional clubs in Wales should remain at four. Derbies: The report claims fixtures between the four Welsh clubs generated 48% of league attendances at home games in Wales from 2012 to 2026. With three clubs, those fixtures would fall from 12 derbies a season to six. Players: Removing one team would create what the report calls a "bottleneck", with fewer elite playing opportunities in Wales and a greater risk of more Welsh players moving to clubs outside Wales. Wales: The report finds that Wales have recorded higher Six Nations finishes in the seasons when the Welsh clubs have performed well. All four clubs contribute: Over the period the report records Cardiff with the highest average attendances, Scarlets as the leading Welsh club in the European Cup and Dragons with the highest stadium utilisation, alongside the Ospreys' record in the league and in supplying most players to Wales and the Lions. What has not been included in great depth in the initial findings are the financial constraints or how keeping four teams can be afforded. The WRU has reported recent losses of £18m and says it has to reduce its spend on professional rugby from £26m to £20m by 2028. The four sides currently receive about £6.5m each. The Ospreys report follows the Keystone report that was commissioned by the WRU who said it outlined data why Welsh rugby needs to cut a side. sports.description: New Zealand kept the series alive with a commanding 244-run win over India in Friday's fourth one-day international at Mount Maunganui, driven by a century from Will Young and a six-wicket haul by Matt Henry, who dismissed the touring side for 89. Although trailing 2-1 in the five-match contest and unable to claim an overall series victory, the home team can still secure a draw should they win Sunday’s final fixture at the same ground. Rain had forced the abandonment of the third game. Set a target of 334, India endured a terrible start when fast bowler Henry reduced them to 0-3 during a devastating opening over, dismissing Rohit Sharma , Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer in quick succession. Ruturaj Gaikwad was removed soon after, though a stubborn 44-run stand between Ishan Kishan (27) and Axar Patel (21), alongside a rapid 21 from Naman Dhir, prevented India from suffering a record-breaking run defeat. Henry claimed three further victims to wrap up the innings, bowling India out for their sixth-lowest total in ODI history. Will Young celebrating hitting a century off 88 balls (Getty) At the start of the day, opener Young recovered from earlier scores of 9 and 6 in the series to make a career-best 125 off 108 balls to the gall of India who dropped him twice on the way to registering his fifth century in the format. The 33-year-old capitalised on sloppy Indian fielding after Rohit and Kishan dropped catches off consecutive balls during the second over of the innings. Young received solid support from Tim Seifert, who scored 58, and Finn Allen, who added 41, while India's bowling attack saw Patel, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi take two wickets apiece. sports.description: Tottenham consider January loan recall for Mikey Moore amid Rangers return talk Expectations were high when Mikey Moore joined 1. Moore is still waiting for his first goal in Germany, having started six of the nine games he has played in all competitions for the Billy Goats. Given Moore's struggles to establish himself in the Bundesliga, Tottenham and Köln could agree to terminate his loan six months early in January, according to a report from TEAMtalk. Such a move would allow Spurs to explore alternative options for the teenager in a bid to find him a destination that would be a better fit than Köln has been so far. Moore enjoyed great success at Rangers last season, but the Scottish side are not actively pursuing a return for him. sports.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
sports.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. sports.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. sports.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
sports.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. sports.title: Curtis Jones breaks silence on Liverpool exit – “I want to win”
sports.description: Curtis Jones breaks silence on Liverpool exit – “I want to win” Curtis Jones Targets Trophies at Inter Milan After Liverpool Exit Curtis Jones has moved on from Liverpool, and the reasoning is straightforward. At 25, after eight seasons around the first team and plenty of silverware, he wanted something bigger in his own career, a central role in a side built to win immediately. Inter Milan offered that. His Liverpool record stands up well enough. Jones made 228 appearances, scored 22 goals and supplied 22 assists. He collected two Premier League titles, the FA Cup, two League Cups and the FIFA Club World Cup. Those are serious honours by any measure. But footballers do not judge their careers only by what they won, they judge them by when and how much they were trusted. That is where the picture changes. Jones was an unused substitute in the FA Cup final, the Club World Cup final and Liverpool’s 2022 Champions League final defeat to Real Madrid. He also missed the matchday squads for the 2022 and 2024 League Cup finals, with injury keeping him out of the latter. For a home-grown midfielder at his boyhood club, that matters. Inter Milan move built on ambition Inter are not offering nostalgia, they are offering a project with recent evidence behind it. Three Serie A titles, three Coppa Italia triumphs and two Champions League final appearances in the past five years tell the story clearly enough. Jones has joined a club that expects to compete for major honours every season. He has made his priorities clear too. “Simply winning. I want to win,” he said when asked about his objective in Milan. “I want to be part of a winning team. “I have great faith in the guys around me. I don’t want to be the one who just says: ‘I want to score all the goals, I want to make all the assists’. “Of course, I want to score, make assists, and help the team. But the quality of the players I’ve seen around me is extraordinary. I know opportunities like this will come. “But above all, I want to be part of a winning team, come in and make my contribution.” Liverpool exit carried emotional weight There is no need to pretend this was an easy departure. Jones made that plain. “It makes me feel really good to know that such a great team has placed their trust in me, giving me the chance to come here and be part of the team. Because, in any case, my choice has always been Inter. “I know the club’s history, the players, the great champions, and everyone who has worn this shirt. But I’ve always been a Liverpool boy, I’ve always been attached to my club and its history. technology.title: Palantir's NHS cancer app gets plenty of praise, precious few users
technology.description: Only a handful of NHS trusts are using the cancer app on the controversial £330 million Federated Data Platform (FDP) run by Palantir, while newly released figures raise questions about which trusts are benefiting. Cancer 360 was designed to bring cancer patients' data from disparate spreadsheets and electronic health records into a central system, helping health professionals prioritize treatment. Pilots began four years ago, and trusts are not charged directly for the FDP. Yet official figures put Cancer 360's uptake at just five or six trusts. Freedom of Information responses gathered by grassroots campaign group No Palantir in the NHS also reveal discrepancies between reported benefits and recorded use. In June 2025, NHS England said that Cancer 360 "drastically cut down diagnosis times" and referred to a pilot at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, which saw the proportion of patients diagnosed within 28 days climb from 72 percent to 85 percent. The trust began trials in 2022, while working with Palantir under a £23 million contract awarded without competition, before the US firm was awarded the FDP contract in late 2023. Critics argued the FDP procurement was flawed as Palantir had developed use cases under £60 million in non-competitive contracts which were then carried over to the FDP. Last year, NHS England said Cancer 360 served 46 registered teams and 239 active users, and processed 52,000 patients. In June 2026, NHS England said there were five trusts using Cancer 360 as of March 2026. Of those, only two were listed as benefiting. In July, health minister Preet Kaur Gill repeated the five-trust usage figure in a Parliamentary answer . Official data released in October said that as of June, six trusts were using Cancer 360 and five were benefiting, but did not identify the trusts or explain the increase. The stats have since been removed from the NHS England website but are archived here . In June, NHS England responded to a Freedom of Information request . It said six trusts reported unique users logging into the Cancer 360 app over the last 12 months. However, two trusts cited as having run successful pilots – Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and Royal United Hospitals Bath – were listed as having zero unique users logging into the system during that period, according to NHS England's reply. Both trusts were said to have received benefits from the system, according to a FoI response sent to campaign group Foxglove in June this year. The Register asked both trusts and NHS England to explain the discrepancy. One of the six trusts said to be logging into the cancer app, East Lancashire Hospitals, reported just one unique user. It later confirmed in an FoI response in August that it was not live with the FDP. It had planned to adopt the platform, leading with Cancer 360, but did not have a date for going live with the app. No Palantir in the NHS also identified trusts that considered Cancer 360 but decided against adopting it.

technology.title: C++26 stumbles at finish line over Contracts dispute
technology.description: The next version of the C++ programming language may be delayed at the last minute due to a dispute over a security-enhancing Contracts feature. Contracts have deeply split C++ technical maintainers. One group backs the C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup , who is against the technology in its present form in grounds it was hastily implemented. But others are eager to see Contracts implemented, even arguing the tech's detractors are poisoning the C++ development process itself. The disagreement boiled over just before a vote to ratify the new version of the language. In October, the Draft International Standard (DIS) of C++26 failed its ISO ballot — the next-to-last stage in the International Organization for Standardization’s approval process during which a standard's technical details are formally ratified by a set of national standards bodies. The ballot saw 13 votes cast in favor, 9 against, and 12 abstentions, failing to meet the ISO requirement of having no more than 25 percent negative votes. Contracts was the major sticking point for those voting nay. Contracts dispute Contracts allow developers to add preconditions and postconditions to code, as well as assertions that check whether specified conditions hold. Such checks can help catch programming errors that might otherwise lead to undefined behavior. Design by Contract has long been a feature of languages like Ada and Eiffel . Developers have proposed adding Contracts to C++ for at least a decade, after when they were abruptly yanked from C++20 owing to concerns over dangerous defaults. But Stroustrup roasted the revised proposal ( P2900 ) that made it into C++26. “The P2900 contracts and extensions aim to change the nature of C++ and are an existential threat to C++, adding complexity and bloat,” Stroustrup and his colleagues wrote in a paper last August. They noted that the implementation is messy, outdated, not sufficiently tested , and could be more effectively implemented as a library. Not everyone agrees. Andreas Fertig , a member of the C++ standardization committee, feels that the criticisms have already been vetted and that vetoing the proposal this late in the C++ release process is damaging to C++ itself. “The topic has been worked on for years and has received a majority vote multiple times in its current form.
